definitions.gloss: sitting or riding astride, with one leg on each side
definitions.explanation: The posture of straddling something with a leg on each side, as when riding a horse. Also used adjectivally for garments divided into two leg sections rather than a single skirt-like piece.

examples.japanese: ⟦{子|こ}→子：09851_ko⟧どもは⟦{父親|ちちおや}→父親：03469_chichioya⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{肩|かた}→肩：02192_kata⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{馬乗|うまの}りになった。
examples.english: The child sat astride his father's shoulders.

examples.japanese: ⟦{柵|さく}→柵：13103_saku⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{馬乗|うまの}りになって⟦{座|すわ}った→座る：00757_suwaru⟧。

⟦{剣道|けんどう}→剣道：04452_kendou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{足|あし}→足：00575_ashi⟧さばきのため、{馬乗|うまの}り{袴|ばかま}という{二股|ふたまた}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{分|わ}かれた→分かれる：10976_wakareru⟧⟦{袴|はかま}→袴：02245_hakama⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{履|は}く→履く：00700_haku⟧。
examples.english: In kendo, divided-leg hakama called umanori-bakama are worn for freer footwork.

notes:
⟦{馬|うま}→馬：01865_uma⟧ (horse) + {乗|の}り (riding): literally the posture of riding a horse, extended to any straddling position.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {馬乗|うまの}りになる: to sit/get astride (something)
- {馬乗|うまの}り⟦{袴|はかま}→袴：02245_hakama⟧: divided-leg hakama, cut like wide trousers rather than a skirt, worn for martial arts where free leg movement matters

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{行灯|あんどん}→行灯：20055_andon⟧{袴|ばかま}: undivided, skirt-style hakama — the alternative to {馬乗|うまの}り{袴|ばかま}, common at graduation ceremonies
